L5.1.quote:
For $f(x)=x+c$ ($c\ge 0$) the original inequalities become \[
\sqrt{\frac{x^2 + (y+c)^2}{2}} \ge \frac{x+y+c}{2} \ge \sqrt{x(y+c)} ,
\] which are exactly the Quadratic‑Mean–Arithmetic‑Mean inequality and the Arithmetic‑Mean–Geometric‑Mean inequality applied to the two positive numbers $x$ and $y+c$. Both inequalities are true for all $x,y>0$.
L5.1.note: Both inequalities verified for all x,y and every c ≥ 0; middle term correctly (f(x)+y)/2.

L5.2.quote:
Hence the chain collapses to equality: \[
\bigl(f(f(y)) + y\bigr)^2 = 4f(y)^2 .
\] Taking square roots (all terms are positive) yields \[
f(f(y)) + y = 2f(y) \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
\boxed{f(f(x)) = 2f(x) - x \qquad \forall x>0.}
L5.2.note: Substitution x=f(y) correct; (4) then gives the arithmetic-progression/orbit invariance g(x+g(x))=g(x).

L5.3.note: Nonnegativity of g(t)=f(t)−t is never proved; no orbit-positivity argument appears anywhere.

L5.4.quote: Take $n = q t$, $m = p t$ for $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Then $n c_1 - m c_2 = 0$, so the right‑hand side of (9) is the constant $(u-v-c_2)^2$, while the left‑hand side grows linearly with $t$ (coefficient $2(c_1-c_2)(q c_1 + p c_2) > 0$). For large $t$ the inequality is violated – contradiction.
L5.4.note: Both rational and irrational ratio cases fully written; equivalent iterate-comparison route via derived inequality (7), itself correctly proved.

L5.5.quote: If $x \in S_0$, then by (12) we must have $|x - (u + n c)| > c$ (because $u+nc \in S_c$). This is impossible. Hence $S_0 = \emptyset$.
L5.5.note: Separation |x−y|>c (12) and mixed-case exclusion (Lemma 1, covering) are rigorously proved; but 'V ⊆ {0,c}' is asserted without excluding negative g-values.

parsed.notes: Sufficiency (L5.1) and the structural identity (L5.2) are fully written. Necessity handles equal positive differences and the fixed-point/mixed case rigorously, but never proves g(x)=f(x)−x ≥ 0; the dichotomy 'g≡0 or V⊆{0,c}' ignores possible negative values, so necessity is incomplete as written.
